name: @prometheus/cli
description: prometheus — Prometheus Studio terminal CLI / interactive TUI (Node). Full GUI feature parity over engine-bridge.
//publish-note: CLI-098 (M7): the published tarball ships ONE self-contained file — dist/bin.js — produced by `prepack` = `tsc -b` (build + typecheck the workspace deps) then esbuild bundles src/bin.ts with the @prometheus/* WORKSPACE deps INLINED. Those live in devDependencies (dev gets the pnpm symlink for tsc/tests; publish DROPS devDependencies), so the tarball has NO dangling `workspace:*` and NO registry dependency on the sibling packages. The Ink REPL externals (ink/react/yargs/chalk) are also devDependencies + `--external`: the one-shot CLI + the bundled REPL brain need none of them (bin.ts loads the Ink view via a guarded dynamic import and degrades to the one-shot help when absent), so `dependencies` is empty and `npm i -g` is truly zero-dependency. `files` is a strict whitelist ⇒ src/, *.test.*, *.map, .d.ts, dev-register.mjs, tsconfig NEVER reach the tarball (verify with `pnpm pack --dry-run`). The engine (prometheus.py/nemesis) is NOT bundled — set PROMETHEUS_PY / NEMESIS_BIN or put it on PATH (see README + doctor-bridge.ts).
//deps-note: The @prometheus/* workspace packages + the Ink-REPL externals (ink/react/yargs/chalk) are DEV-only: dev resolves them via the pnpm workspace symlink; the published package bundles the @prometheus/* code into dist/bin.js and loads the (optional) Ink view via a guarded dynamic import. Keeping `dependencies` empty preserves the zero-dependency install the README advertises.
